subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and if so which scope is allowed: warnings only, structured handoff/checkpoint, bounded deferral, or no new surface?
rationale: The request crosses public config, session continuity, workspace writes, and approval/authority boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security contract.

options.title: Adopt warning and handoff only
options.body: Add opt-in pre-threshold warnings plus a structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt full bounded deferral
options.body: Allow warning, handoff, and DEFER only with explicit max duration, audit logging, idempotent checkpoint matching, workspace scope, and approval-expiry rules.

options.title: Keep existing lifecycle surfaces
options.body: Treat memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, context-engine maintenance, and checkpoints as the supported compaction surfaces and route remaining behavior to docs or future design.

recommendation.title: Adopt warning and handoff only
recommendation.body: Add opt-in pre-threshold warnings plus a structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The memoryFlush implementation is the closest current pre-compaction lifecycle behavior and is central to the requested handoff path.
